findings.title: Duplicate `downsize` definition silently drops width/height API
findings.body: File defines `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` at line 145 and then immediately redefines `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` at line 149. Ruby has no overloading, so the second definition overwrites the first. Any existing caller using the 4-arg form (max_width, max_height) will now get wrong arity / misinterpreted arguments and raise ArgumentError or produce a malformed geometry string. The 80% string form needed by uploads_controller should be a separate arity-tolerant method.

findings.title: Loop re-checks stale `tempfile.size` after in-place convert
findings.body: The downsizing loop checks `tempfile.size` before and on each iteration, but `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` rewrites the file via an external `convert` process. The open `tempfile` descriptor still refers to the old inode/size, so `tempfile.size` does not reflect the new on-disk size. The loop can therefore run all 5 iterations even when already small enough, or never terminate early, and the later `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` stores a stale filesize.

findings.title: In-place convert with same source/dest and unchecked failure
findings.body: Call uses `tempfile.path` as both `from` and `to` for `convert from[0] ... to`. Reading and writing the same path in one ImageMagick invocation risks truncating/corrupting the upload if the command fails partway. Return value is also ignored and `attempt` is always decremented, so 5 expensive converts run even when conversion fails, after which an still-oversized file is passed to `Upload.create_for`.

findings.title: Client validation hardcodes 10MB for all upload types
findings.body: validateUploadedFile replaced `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with `10 * 1024`. That lifts the limit for `attachment` uploads as well as `image` uploads, so oversized attachments pass client checks only to be rejected by the server (bad UX and wasted upload), and sites with a lower or higher configured limit get a wrong error message. Only images are auto-downsized server-side, so attachments must still respect their site setting.
